author: United States Strategic Bombing Survey, Naval Analysis Division
title: Interrogations of Japanese Officials
publisher: United States Government Printing Office, Washington
edition: USSBS Reports (Pacific), vols. I–II; 118 interrogations conducted in Tokyo, October–December 1945
notes: Japanese officers questioned in Tokyo within weeks of the surrender, in English translation, with the interrogating officer named and the date and place given for each. Primary in form: it is the transcript, not an account built from it. It is also the earliest layer of the postwar testimony that later became the received Western account, which makes it useful in a particular way — Nav. No. 6 (USSBS No. 40, 18 October 1945) is Fuchida Mitsuo three months after the surrender, and what he says there can be set against what he said in 1948 and 1963 and against the operation orders in source:japanese-monograph-97. Cite it for what a Japanese officer said in 1945, never for what happened.
